mainTopic: When bringing blood or meat inside or outside, or intending to, makes a קרבן פסול, and why the פסוק needs both ״קדש״ and ״פנימה״
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: intent to bring blood into the היכל does not disqualify a קרבן, because the forbidden 'place' must be outside the proper area for blood, meat and אימורים together. A קל וחומר suggests that intent to take blood outside the עזרה should not disqualify either, but the word 'פגול' in the פסוק teaches that it does. A second ברייתא teaches that meat taken outside its area is פסול, while meat brought into the היכל stays כשר. It defends each half with a פסוק: 'מדמה' and 'בשדה'. Next, a ברייתא learns from ״אל הקדש פנימה״ that blood of a חטאת brought into the היכל is פסול, and the גמרא asks why ״פנימה״ is needed. רבא compares it to ״תושב״ and ״שכיר״. אביי challenges the comparison and suggests a roundabout path. רבא rejects that and explains that blood headed for the inner room is not פסול while passing through the היכל. The amud ends with a chain of questions from רבא about blood of inner offerings and of יום הכיפורים that is brought into the קודש הקדשים, and this chain continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The place must count for blood, meat, and altar portions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the 'place' that disqualifies a קרבן through wrong intent must be outside the proper area for all three parts of the קרבן: blood, meat and אימורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The place must be 'threefold': it must apply to the blood, to the meat, and to the altar portions.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its reading of the פסוק. Intent about a 'place' only disqualifies if that place is outside the proper area for blood, meat and אימורים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why intent to bring the blood into the היכל does not make the קרבן פסול. The היכל does not fit the 'threefold' requirement, so intent about it does not disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: Place, here the place the person intends to use for the קרבן
Threefold, applying to all three things together
The parts of the קרבן that are burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: A place that must be threefold
in the blood, in the meat, in the sacrificial portions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's derivation, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intent about a place disqualifies only if that place is outside the proper area for blood, meat and אימורים. So intent to bring the blood into the היכל does not disqualify the קרבן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule sets up the next step's question. If intent about the inside does not disqualify, maybe intent about the outside should not disqualify either.

steps.title: A קל וחומר suggests intent to take the blood outside should not disqualify
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues: inside, blood really does disqualify, yet intent does not. Outside, blood does not disqualify, so surely intent should not disqualify there either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then intent about the outside should not disqualify either, by a קל וחומר. Inside, blood that went in disqualifies the blood left outside, and still intent to bring it inside does not disqualify. Outside, blood that went out does not disqualify the blood left inside. Surely intent to take it outside should not disqualify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges with a קל וחומר. It argues that intent to bring the blood outside the עזרה should also fail to disqualify the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing blood into the היכל is the more serious act, because it even ruins the blood left outside. Yet intent to do it does not disqualify. Taking blood outside is the weaker act, because it does not ruin the blood left inside. So the logic says intent to do it should certainly not disqualify.

keyTerms.meaning: Intent, a wrong plan in mind while doing the עבודה
A 'how much more so' argument, from the stronger case to the weaker one
Inside (the היכל) / outside (the עזרה)
Is it not logical?, a phrase that ends a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'inside' means into the היכל, deeper than normal, and 'outside' means out of the עזרה. Both are wrong places, but in opposite directions.

phrases.english: And let intent about outside not disqualify
by a קל וחומר:
Just as in the place where it disqualifies:
the blood that is inside disqualifies what is outside
and yet intent about inside does not disqualify,
then in the place where it does not disqualify:
the blood that is outside does not disqualify what is inside
is it not logical
that intent about outside should not disqualify?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תְּהֵא מַחְשָׁבָה פּוֹסֶלֶת בַּחוּץ מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the result of step 1 (intent about inside does not disqualify) as the stronger side of a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The accepted rule that intent to take the blood outside the עזרה (חוץ למקומו) disqualifies the קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood inside is the stronger case, because it ruins the outside blood, yet intent about it does not disqualify. Blood outside is the weaker case, because it does not ruin the inside blood. So intent about outside should certainly not disqualify.

steps.title: The פסוק itself teaches intent outside the proper place
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from the פסוק: 'שלישי' refers to intent beyond the proper time, and 'פגול' refers to intent outside the proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says it: 'third' means beyond its time; 'פגול' means outside its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we do not follow the קל וחומר, because the פסוק directly teaches that intent outside the proper place disqualifies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear teaching from the פסוק beats a קל וחומר. The word 'שלישי' (the third day) covers wrong intent about time. The extra word 'פגול' is read as covering wrong intent about place, meaning outside the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches, introducing a source from the תורה
Third, the third day in the פסוק
A קרבן made invalid by wrong intent
Beyond its proper time
Outside its proper place

steps.whatToRemember: Intent about the היכל (inside) does not disqualify, because it fails the 'threefold' rule. Intent about outside the עזרה does disqualify, because the word 'פגול' teaches it, even though a קל וחומר seemed to say otherwise.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'third' refers to beyond its time,
'piggul' refers to outside its place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 2 with a direct source from the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A direct source from the פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the קל וחומר, intent to take the blood outside the עזרה should not disqualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'פגול' explicitly teaches that intent outside the proper place disqualifies, so the קל וחומר does not apply.

steps.title: Meat taken outside is invalid; meat brought inside stays valid
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that meat of a קרבן taken outside its proper area is פסול, but meat brought into the היכל is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meat that goes outside is invalid; meat that goes inside is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that turns from blood to meat. It contrasts meat going out with meat going in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat that leaves its eating area (the walls of ירושלים for קדשים קלים, the עזרה for קדשי קדשים) becomes פסול. Meat that is brought deeper, into the היכל, is not ruined and may still be eaten. This is different from blood of a חטאת, which is ruined by being brought inside.

keyTerms.meaning: That goes out
That comes in
Invalid, not allowed to be eaten
Valid, allowed to be eaten

phrases.english: Meat that goes outside is invalid,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, so read them as part of the line.

phrases.english: meat that enters inside is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of blood and intent to a new ברייתא about meat physically going out or in.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat of a קרבן taken outside its proper area is פסול. Meat brought inside the היכל remains כשר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'inside' and 'outside' work differently for meat than for blood, and the סוגיא will build on this contrast.

steps.title: A logical argument that meat brought into the היכל should be disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a logical argument: if meat is ruined by going outside the courtyard, where the rules on blood are lighter, then surely it should be ruined by going into the היכל, where the rules on blood are stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think logic says meat brought into the היכל is פסול. Outside the courtyard, blood that goes out does not ruin the blood left inside, and still meat that goes out is ruined. Inside the היכל, blood that goes in does ruin the blood left outside. So shouldn't meat that goes in surely be ruined?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own ruling that meat brought into the היכל is כשר by offering a logical argument that it should be פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument compares two places. Going outside the courtyard is 'weaker' for blood, because the blood that left does not ruin the rest. Going into the היכל is 'stronger' for blood, because the blood that went in ruins all of it. If meat is ruined in the weaker case, it should surely be ruined in the stronger case.

keyTerms.meaning: by logic; by reasoning from one case to another
disqualified; not fit to be eaten or offered
that which is outside
that which is inside

steps.confusionAlert: 'Inside' and 'outside' shift meaning here. For meat going out, 'outside' means outside the courtyard (עזרה). For blood or meat going in, 'inside' means into the היכל.

phrases.english: That it should be by logic that it is disqualified:
phrases.notes: Read this as the end of 'one might have thought...': the ברייתא is asking about meat brought into the היכל.

phrases.english: And just as in a place where it does not disqualify
the blood that is outside does not disqualify that which is inside
meat that goes outside is disqualified,

phrases.aramaic: מְקוֹם שֶׁפָּסַל דָּם שֶׁבִּפְנִים אֶת שֶׁבַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: then in a place where the blood that is inside disqualifies that which is outside,
meat that enters inside
is it not logical that it should be disqualified?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of Step 4's ruling (meat in the היכל is כשר) with a logical argument.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that meat brought into the היכל is כשר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: the היכל is stricter for blood than the outside, so if meat is ruined outside it should surely be ruined in the היכל.

steps.title: The word 'מדמה' limits the rule to blood
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'of its blood' is brought inside, which teaches that only the blood is ruined by entering the היכל, not the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'of its blood': its blood is ruined by going in, but not its meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the logical argument with a פסוק that says only blood brought into the היכל is ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clear פסוק overrides a logical argument. Because the פסוק specifically says 'מדמה', the rule that entering the היכל ruins something applies only to blood, so meat that enters stays כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: behold, the פסוק says; introduces a verse that blocks the argument
of its blood
its meat

phrases.english: Behold, the verse says: 'of its blood'
its blood, and not its meat.
phrases.notes: Some versions read 'בשר' (meat) in the round brackets; the square brackets give the corrected wording, 'בשרה' (its meat).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 5's logical argument with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural limitation overrides a logical inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By logic, meat entering the היכל should be פסול like blood.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק says 'מדמה', so only blood is ruined by entering; meat stays כשר.

steps.title: A reverse argument that meat taken outside should be fit
steps.stepSummary: Now that meat in the היכל is כשר, the ברייתא builds a reverse קל וחומר: if meat is fine in the stricter place, it should surely be fine in the lighter place outside the courtyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now we can make a קל וחומר the other way. Inside the היכל, blood that goes in ruins the blood outside, and still meat that goes in is כשר. Outside the courtyard, blood that goes out does not ruin the blood inside. So shouldn't meat that goes out surely be כשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the answer it just gave to build a new argument that challenges the first half of its ruling, that meat taken outside is פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that meat is not ruined in the היכל, the place that is stricter for blood. If meat survives the stricter place, logic says it should survive the lighter place, outside the courtyard. This attacks the rule that meat taken outside is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one, or the reverse
from now; now that this has been established
fit; valid

phrases.english: Now then, a kal vachomer:
And just as in a place where it disqualifies
the blood that is inside disqualifies that which is outside
meat that enters inside is fit,
then in a place where it does not disqualify
the blood that is outside does not disqualify that which is inside
meat that goes outside
is it not logical that it is fit?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 6's conclusion to challenge the other half of Step 4's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that meat taken outside its proper area is פסול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reverse קל וחומר: meat stays כשר in the היכל, which is stricter for blood, so it should surely stay כשר outside, which is lighter for blood.

steps.title: Meat that leaves its boundary becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ובשר בשדה טרפה לא תאכלו' teaches that once meat leaves its allowed boundary, it becomes forbidden, which blocks the reverse קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Meat torn in the field you shall not eat.' Once meat has gone out of its boundary, it becomes forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא blocks the reverse קל וחומר with a פסוק that forbids meat taken outside its boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in the field' teach a general rule: meat that goes beyond the area where it may be eaten becomes forbidden, like טרפה. Because of this פסוק, the logical argument fails, and the ruling of Step 4 stands on both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: torn; meat that is forbidden to eat
in the field; outside its proper place
boundary; the area in which the meat may be eaten
becomes forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Two פסוקים set the rule. 'מדמה' means only blood is ruined by entering the היכל, so meat there stays כשר. 'בשדה' means meat that leaves its boundary becomes forbidden. Logic alone could have pushed either way, so the פסוקים decide.

phrases.english: Behold, the verse says:
'And meat torn in the field you shall not eat'
once the meat has gone out
outside its boundary, it becomes forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: וּבָשָׂר בַּשָּׂדֶה טְרֵפָה לֹא תֹאכֵלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 7's reverse קל וחומר with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source overrides a logical inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By reverse קל וחומר, meat taken outside should be כשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בשדה' teaches that meat leaving its boundary becomes forbidden, so it is פסול.

steps.title: Blood brought into the Sanctuary is also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״אל הקדש פנימה״ that a חטאת is פסול if its blood is brought into the היכל, not only into the innermost place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The פסוק says "within." From that word alone I would only know about the innermost place. How do I know the same is true for the היכל? The פסוק says: "Into the sacred place within."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to blood of a חטאת that was carried inside, and quotes a ברייתא. The ברייתא shows that bringing the blood into the היכל ruins it too, not only bringing it into the innermost room.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״פנימה״ by itself would only point to the innermost place, the קודש הקדשים. The added words ״אל הקדש״ stretch the rule to cover the היכל as well. So any inside place ruins the blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Within, meaning the innermost place
The Sanctuary, the building in front of the קודש הקדשים
The Holy of Holies, the innermost room
The פסוק says, introducing the source

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "Within" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18. משה is asking אהרן why the חטאת wasn't eaten, since its blood was not brought inside.

phrases.english: I have only "within,"
phrases.notes: Here 'within' means the innermost place, the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: from where do we know the Sanctuary?
The verse states: "Into the sacred place within."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פְּנִימָה – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא פְּנִימָה, הֵיכָל מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the topic of blood entering inside, which came up in step 6, and gives the full source for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood of a חטאת that is brought into the היכל, and not only into the קודש הקדשים, makes the offering פסול.

steps.title: Why does the verse need the word 'within'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק needs ״פנימה״ at all, since ״קדש״ alone would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק just say "sacred place" and not say "within"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: if the היכל already ruins the blood, why mention the inner room at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the outer room, the היכל, makes the blood פסול, then surely the more holy inner room does too. So the word ״פנימה״ seems to add nothing. The גמרא is asking about extra wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it say... and not say. A way of asking why a word is in the פסוק
The sacred place, here referring to the היכל

phrases.english: And let it say "sacred place,"
and not say "within"!
phrases.notes: If the outer room already ruins the blood, the inner room surely does, so why write it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording the ברייתא in step 9 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra word ״פנימה״ in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the היכל to the more holy inner room makes ״פנימה״ unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא: Each word explains the other
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the two words teach about each other, just like ״תושב״ and ״שכיר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This word comes and teaches about that word. It is just like the case of "tenant and hired worker."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: ״פנימה״ is not extra, because it shows us what ״קדש״ means. He then points to a similar case, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק only said ״קדש״, we would have thought it meant the קודש הקדשים, and we would not know about the היכל. Writing ״פנימה״ next to it shows that ״קדש״ here means the היכל. So each word helps explain the other.

keyTerms.meaning: This comes and teaches about that: one word explains the other
Just as it is with, introducing a similar case

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the קל וחומר is wrong. He is saying that without ״פנימה״ we would have read ״קדש״ as the inner room, so there would be no היכל case to build a קל וחומר from.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּא זֶה וְלִימֵּד עַל זֶה;
phrases.english: Rava said: This comes and teaches about that;
phrases.notes: ״פנימה״ shows that ״קדש״ here means the היכל. Without it we would have read ״קדש״ as the inner room.

phrases.english: just as it is with "tenant and hired worker."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בָּא זֶה וְלִימֵּד עַל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word is needed to explain the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״פנימה″ looked extra, since a קל וחומר from the היכל would cover the inner room.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without ״פנימה″, ״קדש″ would have meant the קודש הקדשים. ״פנימה״ is needed to show that ״קדש״ means the היכל.

steps.title: The parallel case: tenant and hired worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: ״תושב״ is a permanent עבד עברי and ״שכיר״ is one bought for six years. Neither may eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "Tenant" means a slave bought permanently. "Hired worker" means a slave bought for a set number of years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that רבא pointed to, so we can see the similar case. First it defines the two words in the פסוק about who may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a כהן's ״תושב״ and ״שכיר״ may not eat תרומה. The ברייתא explains that ״תושב״ is an עבד עברי who stays until יובל, and ״שכיר״ is one who serves the regular six years.

keyTerms.meaning: Tenant, here meaning a permanent עבד עברי
Hired worker, here meaning an עבד עברי bought for six years
A permanent acquisition, until יובל
An acquisition for a set number of years

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Tenant" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10, about who may not eat a כהן's תרומה.

phrases.english: this is one acquired as a permanent acquisition,
"Hired worker" – this is one acquired for years.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: תּוֹשָׁב – זֶה קָנוּי קִנְיַן עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the comparison רבא made in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״תושב״ refers to an עבד עברי bought permanently, and ״שכיר״ to one bought for years. Neither may eat his master's תרומה.

steps.title: Why mention the hired worker at all?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why ״שכיר״ is needed, since if a permanent slave may not eat תרומה, a temporary one surely may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the פסוק say "tenant" and not say "hired worker." I would have reasoned: if a slave bought permanently does not eat תרומה, then surely a slave bought for years does not!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the quoted ברייתא, a question is raised that looks just like the one in step 10. This sets up the next move; the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanent slave is more tied to the כהן than a six-year slave. So if even the permanent one cannot eat תרומה, a כל שכן says the temporary one cannot either. That makes ״שכיר״ look extra, just as ״פנימה״ looked extra before.

keyTerms.meaning: And I would say, meaning I could have reasoned it on my own
All the more so, a קל וחומר argument

steps.confusionAlert: This question is part of the quoted ברייתא, not a new attack on רבא. It is the same pattern as step 10, and its answer will show how רבא's idea works.

phrases.english: Let it say "tenant" and not say "hired worker,"
and I would say:
one acquired permanently does not eat,
phrases.notes: He means he does not eat his master's תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: קָנוּי קִנְיַן שָׁנִים לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן?
phrases.english: one acquired for years, not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: יֹאמַר תּוֹשָׁב וְאַל יֹאמַר שָׂכִיר, וַאֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 12 by asking why one of its two words is needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כל שכן from the permanent slave to the temporary slave would make ״שכיר״ unnecessary.

steps.title: Without ״שכיר״ we would misread ״תושב״
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that without ״שכיר״, we would think ״תושב״ means a six-year slave, and a permanent slave could eat תרומה. ״שכיר״ shows that ״תושב״ is the permanent one, and neither may eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק only said ״תושב״, I would think it means a slave bought for some years, and a permanent slave may eat. So ״שכיר״ comes and teaches about ״תושב״: one is permanent and one is for years, and neither eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question from step 13. It explains that ״שכיר״ is needed to show us what ״תושב״ really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״תושב״ alone is unclear. It could mean the six-year slave. Once ״שכיר״ (clearly the shorter-term worker) is written, ״תושב״ must mean the permanent נרצע, so both are forbidden to eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanent acquisition: a slave owned until יובל (the נרצע)
Acquisition for years: a slave bought for six years
Came and taught: one word explains the meaning of another

steps.whatToRemember: This is the model רבא uses: two words in a פסוק can explain each other, so neither one is extra.

phrases.english: If it were so, I would say:
phrases.notes: "So" means if the פסוק had written only ״תושב״ without ״שכיר״.

phrases.english: "Tenant" means one acquired for years,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קְנוּי קִנְיַן עוֹלָם יְהֵא אוֹכֵל;
phrases.english: but one acquired permanently may eat;
so "hired worker" came and taught about "tenant,"
that this one is acquired permanently

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה קָנוּי קִנְיַן שָׁנִים – וְאֵינוֹ אוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: and that one is acquired for years, and he does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question of why ״שכיר״ is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining an unclear word through its neighbor
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״תושב״ alone would mean a six-year slave, and a permanent slave could eat תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שכיר״ shows ״תושב״ is the permanent slave, so both are forbidden.

steps.title: אביי: the slave case is not like the blood case
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the comparison fails. ״תושב״ and ״שכיר״ are two different people, and the תורה sometimes writes a קל וחומר anyway. But here the same blood must pass through the היכל first, so once it is פסול there, why mention the inner room?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רבא: There, they are two different people. Even if the פסוק could have written only the נרצע and learned the other by קל וחומר, the תורה sometimes takes the trouble to write it anyway. But here, since the blood is already פסול in the היכל, why do we need the innermost room?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer from step 11. He says the ״תושב״/״שכיר״ example does not fit our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With slaves, there are two separate people, so writing both is just the תורה spelling out a קל וחומר. With blood, it is one blood traveling one path: it reaches the היכל before the קודש הקדשים. It is already פסול on the way, so ״פנימה״ seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Two bodies: two separate people or cases
A slave whose ear was pierced, who stays until יובל
Reasoning from a weaker case to a stronger one
The פסוק took the trouble to write it anyway
The innermost room: the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
It makes sense there, since they are two separate people;

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דַּהֲוָה לֵיהּ לִקְרָא לְמִכְתַּב
phrases.english: and even though the verse could have written
"a pierced slave may not eat,"
and the other would be learned by a קל וחומר,
still, a matter that can be learned by a קל וחומר
the verse sometimes takes the trouble to write out.
But here, since it is already disqualified in the Sanctuary,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets, here and in the next line. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: why is the innermost room needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's comparison now that the ברייתא's reasoning has been laid out.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's answer in step 11 that ״קדש״ and ״פנימה״ teach about each other like ״תושב״ and ״שכיר״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two separate people can both be written down. But one blood always passes the היכל first, so ״פנימה״ seems to add nothing.

steps.title: אביי: ״פנימה״ is for blood that took a roundabout path
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers his own answer: ״פנימה״ is needed for blood that reached the קודש הקדשים without passing through the היכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: ״פנימה״ is needed only for blood brought in by a roundabout way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his own answer to why ״פנימה״ is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood skipped the היכל, for example coming in from above, it never became פסול in the היכל. So we need ״פנימה״ to teach that reaching the קודש הקדשים by itself makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: A roundabout path, not the normal way in through the היכל
It is needed only for

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It is needed only for a roundabout way.
phrases.notes: He means blood that got into the קודש הקדשים without passing through the היכל, for example from the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting רבא's answer, אביי offers a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the פסוק to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blood always passes the היכל, so ״פנימה״ seems extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״פנימה״ covers blood that skipped the היכל and went straight into the קודש הקדשים.

steps.title: רבא: the פסוק speaks of normal bringing
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's answer, because the פסוק uses the word "brought," which means bringing in the normal way, not a roundabout path.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But the word "bringing" is written in the פסוק!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי's answer from step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ״הן לא הובא את דמה אל הקדש פנימה״. "Brought" describes carrying the blood in the regular way, through the היכל. So ״פנימה״ cannot be talking only about an unusual roundabout path.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing: the פסוק's word ״הובא״, meaning carried in the usual way

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But "bringing" is written in it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's roundabout-path answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects אביי's answer from step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word "brought" points to the normal way of bringing, not a roundabout path.

steps.title: רבא: passing through on the way inside does not make it פסול
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: if the כהן means to bring the blood into the קודש הקדשים, it is not פסול just from passing through the היכל. So ״פנימה״ is needed to make it פסול once it reaches the inner room.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Whenever the כהן is planning to bring it into the innermost room, it is not disqualified in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to why ״פנימה״ is needed, which also defends the need for both words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי assumed the blood is already פסול as it passes through the היכל. רבא says no: if the כהן's goal is the inner room, passing through the היכל is only the way there and does not make it פסול. So the פסוק must teach separately that reaching the קודש הקדשים makes it פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended it: the כהן's plan for where the blood goes
It does not become disqualified

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, both ״קדש״ and ״פנימה״ are needed. Blood heading to the inner room is not פסול on the way through the היכל, so the inner room needs its own source.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying blood in the קודש הקדשים is fine. He is only saying that passing through the היכל on the way inside does not make it פסול yet.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מִידֵּי דְּחַשֵּׁיב עֲלֵיהּ לִפְנַי וְלִפְנִים –
phrases.english: Any case where he intended it for the innermost room
is not disqualified in the Sanctuary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new reason why ״פנימה״ is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Intention decides whether passing through counts
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The blood is already פסול as it passes through the היכל, so ״פנימה״ is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blood heading to the inner room is not פסול in the היכל, so ״פנימה״ is needed to make it פסול inside.

steps.title: רבא asks about היכל offerings brought into the inner room
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if the blood of the פר העלם דבר של ציבור or the שעיר עבודה זרה was brought into the קודש הקדשים, is it פסול?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: The bull for a communal mistake and the goat for idol worship, if their blood was brought into the innermost room, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new question. The גמרא is setting up a discussion, and the next step lays out the two sides of his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These offerings are already meant to have their blood sprinkled inside, in the היכל. So the rule about outer חטאות brought inside may not fit them. רבא wants to know whether going one step further, into the קודש הקדשים, makes them פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked: introduces an open question
The bull brought when the community sinned by mistake following a wrong ruling
The goat brought for a communal mistake involving idol worship
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked:
The bull for a communal mistake
and the goat for idol worship,
if he brought their blood into the innermost room, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from outer חטאות to inner ones, asking whether bringing their blood further inside makes them פסול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does bringing the blood of a היכל offering into the קודש הקדשים make it פסול?

steps.title: Two sides of רבא's question about inner-room blood
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains his question. Maybe ״אל הקודש פנימה״ is one package, so ״פנימה״ only disqualifies blood where ״אל הקודש״ also does. Or maybe the blood is פסול simply because the קודש הקדשים is not its proper place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say that the פסוק ״אל הקודש פנימה״ is one unit? Then wherever we read ״אל הקודש״ we also read ״פנימה״, and wherever we do not read ״אל הקודש״ we do not read ״פנימה״. Or perhaps it is פסול because the inner room is not their place?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lays out the two possible ways to answer the question he asked in Step 19.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of these sacrifices is supposed to go into the היכל, so bringing it into the היכל cannot make it פסול. Side one: ״פנימה״ is tied to ״אל הקודש״, so where ״אל הקודש״ does not apply, ״פנימה״ does not apply either, and the blood stays כשר. Side two: the קודש הקדשים is simply the wrong place for this blood, so it is פסול anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say...? (opens the first side of a question)
'Into the holy place, within' (ויקרא 10:18)
We read (we apply the פסוק to this case)
Or perhaps (opens the second side)
Not in their proper place

steps.confusionAlert: ״אל הקודש״ here means the היכל and ״פנימה״ means the קודש הקדשים. For these sacrifices the היכל is the correct place, which is why the first side says the rule never kicks in.

phrases.english: Do we say: 'Into the holy place, within'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 10:18. He reads the two parts of the פסוק as one connected phrase.

phrases.english: anywhere that we read 'into the holy place'
we read for it 'within';
anywhere that we do not read 'into the holy place'
we do not read 'within';
or perhaps it is not their place?
phrases.notes: Meaning the קודש הקדשים is not the right spot for this blood, so it becomes פסול anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question asked in Step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the ״פנימה״ disqualification linked to ״אל הקודש״, or does any blood brought to a place that is not its own become פסול?

steps.title: יום הכיפורים blood brought back into the inner room
steps.stepSummary: Assume the answer is 'not its place.' Now take the פר and שעיר of יום הכיפורים. The כהן גדול sprinkled their blood on the בדים, took it out to the היכל, and then brought it back in. What is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it is פסול because it is not their place: the bull and goat of יום הכיפורים, where he sprinkled from their blood on the poles, then took it out to the היכל and brought it back in, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא builds a follow-up question. It only matters if we accept the second side of the previous question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being in the wrong place makes blood פסול, we must ask what counts as 'its place.' This blood normally belongs in the קודש הקדשים. But here the sprinkling there was already finished, and then the blood was brought in a second time.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (opens a follow-up question)
The bull and goat of יום הכיפורים, whose blood is sprinkled inside the קודש הקדשים
The poles of the ארון
He sprinkled
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמָן הוּא –
phrases.english: And if you say it is not their place,
the bull and goat of Yom Kippur
where he sprinkled from their blood on the poles,
and took them out to the Sanctuary and brought them in, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא בִּמְקוֹמָן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the second side of Step 20 and asks a deeper follow-up question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is יום הכיפורים blood that already finished its sprinkling in the קודש הקדשים made פסול by being brought back in?

steps.title: Is it still its place, or did leaving end that?
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains both sides. Maybe the קודש הקדשים is still this blood's place. Or maybe once it went out, it is out, and the inner room is no longer its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say it is its place? Or perhaps, since it went out, it went out?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא lays out the two sides of the יום הכיפורים question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: this blood belongs in the קודש הקדשים, so bringing it back is not 'the wrong place.' Side two: once the job inside is done and the blood has left, it has lost its connection to that room. Bringing it back would then be like bringing it to a wrong place.

keyTerms.meaning: It is their place
Since it went out, it went out (it has left for good)

phrases.english: Do we say it is their place,
or perhaps, since it went out, it went out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two sides of the question in Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does leaving the קודש הקדשים after finishing the sprinkling end the blood's link to that place?

steps.title: Setting up the next question: sprinkling on the curtain
steps.stepSummary: Now assume 'once out, it is out.' רבא starts a new case where the blood was sprinkled on the פרוכת. The question continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say, since it went out, it went out: if he sprinkled from their blood on the curtain...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next question in רבא's chain. Here it only begins the case of sprinkling on the פרוכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each question in the chain assumes the answer to the one before it. This one assumes that blood which left the קודש הקדשים loses its place there. The full case and question about the פרוכת come next.

keyTerms.meaning: The curtain between the היכל and the קודש הקדשים

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר הוֹאִיל וּנְפַק נְפַק –
phrases.english: And if you say, since it went out, it went out,
if he sprinkled from their blood on the curtain,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר הוֹאִיל וּנְפַק נְפַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the second side of Step 22 and begins a further follow-up case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Setup: what happens when the blood was sprinkled on the פרוכת (the question continues on the next amud).
